title: From the Editor
summary: Full-page composition: Atmospheric editorial splash over a rainy Harbor Phase that visibly works: raised transit, flood-control gates, occupied windows, umbrellas, freight movement, wet sidewalks and practical city light. Keep the lower-right city detail clear and leave a broad calm field of rain-dark sky and glass reflection for the full editor letter. No core-character faces.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to Low Tide.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This story begins in a city that works.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Harbor Phase adapted. The water rose, the city moved, the systems got better, and ordinary life continued. People have jobs. Apartments. Bars they have been going to for years. Friends they have known too long. The machines usually do what they are supposed to do.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Nobody needs saving.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That matters.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Because the six people you are about to meet are not running from a ruined world. They are living inside a successful one. They like their lives, mostly. They like each other, mostly. And each of them has a slightly different reason to wonder whether mostly is enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Beyond the floodwall, there are places the ocean only gives back for a few hours at a time.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: People have started going out there.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They have names for the routes. Stories about what they have found. Arguments about how far you can get before the tide turns. Most of it sounds exaggerated.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Probably.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Issue #1 starts with six old friends, one unusually low tide, and the kind of invitation that becomes much harder to dismiss once somebody asks:

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: You going tonight?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They have jobs in the morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They know the water comes back.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And none of them actually knows what is waiting on the other side of the flats.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Turn the page.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page rainy Harbor Phase cityscape with real civic life and functioning infrastructure. Reserve a large quiet vertical text field in rain-dark sky and reflected glass; body copy reads cleanly in restrained editorial blocks, with FROM THE EDITOR small at top, YOU GOING TONIGHT? given one strong display beat, and TURN THE PAGE isolated at bottom. No cover trade dress, no character lineup, no decorative cyberpunk UI.

title: From the Editor
summary: Full-page composition: Exterior of the unfinished dead mall at low tide, wet concrete and black water below, one or two practical work lights glowing on an upper level, fog swallowing the far structure. Leave the darkest facade and fog field open for editorial copy. No identifiable core characters.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Last time, the impossible turned out to have work lights, noodle cups, wall marks, and people who already knew where to stand.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That changes things.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A ruin is something you visit.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A place with routes, regulars, and jokes is something you can start belonging to.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The six still know the tide comes back. Ryan still watches the water when everyone else looks up. Nicole still wants to see the rest. Chris is already turning moments into stories. Justin wants the higher ledge. Matt likes knowing where to go next. Kevin keeps noticing the parts nobody wants to calculate out loud.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: None of that is a problem yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Probably.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The dangerous part of Tide Town is not that it is empty.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It is that it is getting familiar.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Turn the page.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page dead-mall exterior with wet concrete, black tidal water, dim upper-level work lights and fog. Keep the architecture looming but readable, with negative space in the dark facade and fog for a restrained editor letter. Emphasize the sentence IT IS THAT IT IS GETTING FAMILIAR as the final visual beat before TURN THE PAGE.

title: From the Editor
summary: Full-page composition: Quiet pre-dawn apartment threshold with a packed tide-run bag, wet boots, charged battery pack and jacket by the door while an ordinary kitchen sits undisturbed behind them. City rain glows beyond a window. Leave clean wall and shadow space for editorial copy; no people visible.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The first trip was an expedition.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The second had a route.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now they are close to having a routine.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is how strange things become normal: somebody knows where to park, somebody remembers the good stairwell, somebody brings the extra battery, somebody says, “same time?”

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tide Town is still dangerous. The water has not changed. The buildings have not become more stable.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The people have changed.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They know enough to stop feeling like visitors.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And not nearly enough to know what that will cost them.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Turn the page.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page still life at an apartment door before dawn: packed tide bag, wet boots, charged light, jacket and ordinary domestic space beyond. Use natural gray-blue practical light and leave a broad clean wall/shadow field for text. The visual joke is that expedition gear now looks as routine as keys by the door.

title: From the Editor
summary: Full-page composition: Editorial still-life montage of ordinary inland obligations crowded by tide-run preparation: work badge, transit pass, coffee, damp gloves, charging headlamp, folded rain shell, printed tide chart and a bag already repacked. Keep the image grounded and non-infographic, with quiet negative space for copy.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tide Town used to interrupt their lives.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now their lives are starting to organize around Tide Town.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is different.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The six are still working. Still paying rent. Still seeing other people. Still living in a city that works.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: But the next tide is always somewhere in the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Matt, the place is competence.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Justin, attention.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Chris, a story worth telling.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Nicole, the next thing she has not seen yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Kevin, a pattern that keeps getting harder to dismiss.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Ryan, water.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Just water.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And water does not care what the place means to anybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Turn the page.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: One full-page grounded still-life montage rather than a diagram: work and household objects physically crowded by damp tide gear and a printed tide chart. Use wet gray-blue morning light, restrained sodium reflection and clean negative space for the editor copy. No floating UI, no dossier labels, no character portraits.

title: From the Editor
summary: Full-page composition: Predawn floodwall staging lot on an unusually low-tide night, more parked cars and anonymous runner headlamps than usual, the exposed route stretching farther into fog beyond the barrier. Practical vehicle and contractor light only. Reserve sky and wet pavement reflection for editorial copy.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Some dangerous things announce themselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This one looks like a perfect night.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The tide is going out farther.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The route is open longer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: More people are coming.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Everyone has done this before.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Experience feels a lot like safety right up until the conditions stop matching the memory.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The group has spent months learning Tide Town.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ryan has spent the same months learning how little that means to the water.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tonight, those two kinds of knowledge are going to share the same route.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Turn the page.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page threshold scene with the floodwall staging lot busier than earlier crossings, anonymous runners reduced to small silhouettes and headlamps, cars and contractor lights on wet asphalt, and a dramatically exposed route receding into fog. Keep all core cast unidentifiable. Place copy in the sky and dark pavement reflection without blocking the route.

title: From the Editor
summary: Full-page composition: After-hours bar table in Harbor Phase with six places implied by chairs and glasses, one chair conspicuously empty, several phones face-down or glowing with blurred non-readable video thumbnails, rain on the window and no people present. Leave wall/window darkness for editorial copy.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One person did not come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is the only fact that matters to his friends.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Online, it is already becoming something else.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A story.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A warning.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A spectacle.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Proof of whatever the person posting already believed about Tide Town.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The group helped build the mythology around this place. Now the mythology is going to explain them back to themselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Matt wants something he can fix. Chris has footage he no longer knows what to do with. Justin has an audience he suddenly does not want. Nicole still knows why she kept going. Kevin knows the numbers were never the whole problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And somewhere underneath all of it is the question none of them can answer:

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: What did they think the place was giving them?

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Turn the page.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page empty bar-table composition after closing: six chairs around the familiar table, one visibly empty, abandoned glasses, wet coats on hooks and several phones with blurred non-readable clips. Rain and Harbor Phase practical light outside. Keep the human absence central and reserve the dark window/wall for copy; do not depict any core character.

title: From the Editor
summary: Full-page composition: The flats at the start of another extreme low tide, quiet and nearly empty, with a narrow trail of recent footprints leading away from Harbor Phase toward the distant offshore district. Dawn-blue fog, black mud, shallow teal channels and no visible people. Large atmospheric negative space for copy.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They have already crossed for curiosity.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For status.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For competence.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For a story.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For each other.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This time, none of those reasons is enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The place has lost its glow. The mythology has burned off. What remains is concrete, water, distance, and whatever they have not been willing to admit about why they kept returning.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The tide is going low again.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Maybe for the last time that matters.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Going back would be stupid.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not going back would leave the question intact.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So they make one more crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not to find Tide Town.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: To see what is left when they stop asking it to be anything else.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Turn the page.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page flats landscape in dawn-blue fog with black mud, shallow teal water channels and a narrow trail of footprints heading offshore. Harbor Phase is dim behind; the district is only a distant silhouette ahead. No people visible. Use the open fog and sky as the copy field, keeping the footprints as the page-turn vector.
